title: Page-mode immersive header overlaps the first body line
symptom: On a Pixel 8 / Android 14 emulator in page mode, the lightweight immersive header could collide with the first visible body line. A real imported TXT showed the header bottom at y=253 while the first body line started at y=248 before the fix.
root_cause: Page mode used a 44dp base top padding for page text. That converted to a text top that sat above the measured bottom of the immersive header on the current device, while scroll mode already reserved a larger 52dp top band.
fix: Raised the page-mode base top padding from 44dp to 52dp so the first page line clears the immersive header band.
Added an instrumented regression that compares the visible bounds of the immersive header and first body text.
Verified the same real TXT after the fix: the header bottom remained y=253 and the first body line moved to y=269, leaving visible separation.
failed_attempts: Do not rely on static padding values unless they are checked against the actual header bounds on the target device.
Avoid deriving page top padding from the temporary chrome-visible top bar; that can repaginate content when the chrome appears or hides.
impact: Keeps the first page readable in the default page-mode reader and prevents the persistent immersive header from visually pressing into real novel text.
